features: THE GUIDE THAT «ALREADY PAID» WAS MISSING — No migration: the database is not touched. No change in behaviour: what changes is that a feature the program offered without explaining is now explained.

WHAT THE PROBLEM WAS. The «already paid» switch on an expense item opens a whole feature — a list, a page, a dialog — and changes the outcome of the allocation. The only explanation that existed was the description line under the switch itself. All nineteen guides in the program were checked: none explained it, and the «Already paid» page had no guide panel at all.

THE NEW GUIDE IS REACHABLE FROM BOTH PLACES: from the «Guides» menu on the chart of accounts page, where the switch is turned on, and from the «Already paid» page, where the amounts are recorded. It is the same panel: whoever arrives from one side has not seen the other.

IT EXPLAINS WHAT IT IS FOR: you are budgeting a cost the owners had already started paying before this bookkeeping existed. Put it in the budget without saying so and the allocation asks for it all over again; leave it out and the budget no longer matches the accounts. And it says what it is not: not an opening balance, which is the overall picture of a unit's debits and credits.

AND ABOVE ALL IT EXPLAINS TWO BEHAVIOURS NOBODY COULD HAVE KNOWN. First: on an item split between owner and tenant the discount applies to both, because the payment is recorded against the unit and is deducted from the unit's total before that total is divided between the two roles. If only the owner paid, the tenant's share is reduced too. This is not a calculation error: it follows from the data being per unit, and it was already a decision taken and written down in the technical documentation — it was only never told to the people it affects.

SECOND: a share never goes below zero. Anyone who paid more than their part gets no automatic credit — they are asked for zero, and the difference arrives as an Inbox task with the amount unit by unit. That is owners' money sitting somewhere, and what to do with it has to be decided.

PLUS THREE SMALLER POINTS, all verified against the code: turning the switch off does not hide an item you have already recorded payments against; a chapter cannot have «already paid», because the money is recorded where the cost is; and the budget stays whole — what changes is only how much is asked for now, which explains why an instalment plan can add up to less than the budget with nothing wrong.
